initial_presentation: A 10-year-old female patient first visited a neurologist at age 5 due to progressive difficulty in walking and loss of strength. By age 6, she was referred to a geneticist because of challenges in ambulation linked to hypotonia in both lower and upper limbs. Physical examination identified genu valgus and joint hypermobility.

A 22-year-old male patient visited the Department of Oral Medicine and Radiology for a routine dental checkup. His medical and dental histories were unremarkable. Family history indicated recurrent ophthalmic and cardiac issues in his father. General examination showed vital signs within normal limits. The patient exhibited long, slender upper and lower extremities, flat feet, and a thin body habitus with the lower segment of the body being longer than the upper segment. The fingers were long and slender. His height was 164 cm, arm span was 159 cm, and body weight was 47 kg, with an upper to lower segment ratio of 0.75. The chest was flat with prominent ribs, and scoliosis was noted. Wrist and thumb signs were positive. Extraorally, the patient had a long, narrow face with a convex profile. Intraoral examination showed a high arch palate with crowding of the anterior teeth and poor overall periodontal status. Routine blood and urine tests were within normal ranges.

A 72-year-old Caucasian woman presented with a 58-year history of numerous small, reddish and brownish, keratotic papules. These papules initially appeared on her lower limbs and later spread to her upper limbs and trunk. Her medical history was unremarkable for other skin or systemic conditions, except for a well-differentiated cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma in situ on her leg, which was excised two years prior.

A 30-year-old female patient presented with a history of a growth in the upper right molar region for the past 2 months. The mass gradually increased in size and was occasionally associated with pain and bleeding. No swelling or trismus was observed externally. On clinical examination, a 5 cm × 5 cm × 3 cm well-circumscribed, nodular, non-tender, non-fluctuant mass was noted in the distal aspect of the upper right third molar region, extending backward to the pharynx. The right submaxillary lymph nodes were palpable and tender.

A 20-month-old girl from a Taiwanese and Indonesian joint family presented with sudden drowsiness. Upon arrival, she exhibited failure to thrive (FTT), chilblain-like skin lesions, and dystonic posturing with peripheral spasticity.

A 40-year-old Caucasian woman with a history of long-standing joint pain and chronic fatigue syndrome visited the primary care setting for a health maintenance check-up, presenting with new-onset right shoulder pain. The pain started one month ago, characterized by a grinding sensation and a feeling of joint 'displacement' when leaning on her right side. During the review of systems, it was noted that she experiences chronic headaches, joint pain, 'sensitive skin,' and general itchiness. Her past medical history is extensive. Musculoskeletal symptoms include TMJ disorder, chronic joint and muscle pain, low back pain, and repetitive motion injuries. She reported that her pain began around the age of 12. She described lifelong joint injuries, including frequent sprained ankles occurring without any apparent cause.

A 32-day-old female infant presented with a 4-day history of watery diarrhea and fever, experiencing 12-13 episodes of watery stools without mucus or blood in the last 24 hours. There was no history of vomiting, loss of appetite, poor feeding, or respiratory issues. She had been in contact with a confirmed COVID-19 case 4 weeks prior, but no other family members exhibited similar symptoms. The infant was breastfed since birth, born from a nonconsanguineous marriage, and was the second child. Her birth weight was 2700 grams (3–10 percentiles), and she was not premature. Upon admission, she appeared toxic, tachypneic, and irritable with a temperature of 38.4°C (axillary), a pulse rate of 140 beats/minute, a respiratory rate of 30 beats/minute, and blood pressure of 90/60 mmHg. Her weight, height, and head circumference were normal for her age. Physical examination revealed tenting skin turgor, sunken eyes, and a soft fontanelle, while other physical findings were unremarkable. Reflexes and development were normal. She was hospitalized, and empirical antibiotic therapy with ampicillin, cefotaxime, zinc gluconate, and intravenous fluid therapy were initiated.
A 55-year-old male reported experiencing mild visual loss in his right eye over a six-month period.

A 30-year-old Asian male, employed as a school teacher, visited the outpatient neurology department of a tertiary care hospital with a three-month history of left-sided lower back pain. Initially, the pain did not radiate and was alleviated by analgesics. Over the following month, the pain spread to the right lower extremity, increased in severity, and became unresponsive to analgesic treatment. Two weeks later, the patient developed bilateral lower limb weakness and sensory deficits in the L2 region, affecting light touch and pinprick sensations. He did not report any urinary or fecal incontinence. Vital signs were within normal limits.

A 22-month-old girl presented with delayed milestone achievement. The mother's pregnancy was complicated by severe nausea and a urinary tract infection. The baby was delivered at full term via caesarean section due to breech position, with a birth weight of 1800 g. Early neonatal period was marked by feeding difficulties. Subsequently, she developed abdominal distension and multiple vomiting episodes, managed as presumptive sepsis. Physical examination revealed sparse, light-colored scalp hair and reduced muscle tone. She experienced recurrent respiratory infections necessitating frequent antibiotic treatments. At 1 year of age, she had partial head control, could reach for toys, wave bye-bye, and speak single meaningful words. At 22 months, she was evaluated for developmental delay and recurrent vomiting. Anthropometric measurements showed a weight of 6.2 kg and a length of 73 cm, both below the third percentile, with a head circumference of 49.5 cm (97th percentile). Physical examination noted frontal bossing, biparietal prominence, sparse wooly hypopigmented scalp hair, and joint hyperlaxity. She was alert, active, and interacted with her parents. Hypotonia with reduced deep tendon reflexes was also noted.
